0.content: Cyno rescued Collei and brought her to Tighnari. She had Eleazar and had been experimented on by the Fatui under The Doctor, was nearly illiterate, and was terrified of being touched. Tighnari treated her symptoms, began by teaching her to write her own name ("We all start having no knowledge"), and asked her to join the rangers when he saw how keen she was. He calls her a hard worker who puts too much pressure on herself and asks friends to help her. He reads Amber's letters from Mondstadt aloud for her. After Nahida's victory in 3.2 her Eleazar was cured.

1.content: At the Akademiya, Tighnari's popularity drew the General Mahamatra's attention as possible factionalism. Cyno watched him, concluded "an upright and reliable talent... Threat resolved", and they became friends, unusual for a man who keeps his distance from scholars. Cyno visits Gandharva Ville to see Collei and cannot sneak past Tighnari's ears. Cyno respects that Tighnari never crosses the boundaries some scholars cross and supported his refusal of an Akademiya post. Tighnari warns people that being pursued by Cyno for work is the nightmare of a lifetime, and asks him not to joke at the dinner table.

2.content: Naphis, Sage of the Amurta Darshan, was Tighnari's academic adviser and wanted him on the faculty. Tighnari refused, and his master did not push it. He knows Naphis is a man of integrity with a temper, which is why polite Akademiya letters "from my master" made him suspicious. In 3.2 he noticed the letters lacked the weather dots Naphis always draws on the back (one dot for sun, three for rain) and realised something had happened to him. Naphis had been imprisoned for resisting the god-creation plan.

3.comment: Tighnari: The Forest Rangers and Gandharva Ville
3.content: The Forest Rangers protect Avidya Forest's ecology and its visitors, from Withering Zones to careless campers. When Tighnari joined, fresh from Amurta, they were passionate but disorganised. He introduced a patrol log, assigned tasks by strengths and held regular natural-history training. He also teaches visitors survival skills, which the Akademiya technically counts as unauthorised "dissemination of information"; he dares them to stop him. Gandharva Ville is his base, and his hut is where the Traveler woke on arriving in Sumeru.

4.content: An ancestor's manuscript told young Tighnari of the Valuka Shuna. They were a desert people subject to King Deshret, with pale fur and heat-shedding ears, and survived his realm's fall by the Dendro Archon's grace, which turned their fur green. The Aranara named them "large desert dogs" even though they are more like foxes. Tighnari's family inherited some of their traits by living alongside them, and his very dark fur makes him faint in the heat. He notes that his kind are few, scholarly and solitary; his father is an entomologist now studying desert beetles.

5.content: In 3.0 Tighnari explained that the Withering comes from a disease of Irminsul. His ancestors learned this from Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's familiars, though no cure was known. Withering Zones were reappearing faster, killing plants permanently, and Collei's Eleazar grew worse alongside them. He took the Traveler into a zone to destroy its tumours, partly to judge whether they could be trusted with Sumeru's fate. His ancestors had sworn to protect the nation with the Dendro Archon, and he feels that duty is now his. After Nahida's victory the Withering stopped spreading, though existing zones remain work for the rangers.

6.comment: Tighnari: The Doctor, Haypasia and Pardis Dhyai
6.content: The scholar Haypasia went mad after contacting the "newborn god" through meditation. Tighnari secretly moved her to Pardis Dhyai for treatment so the matra would not exile her to Aaru Village. In 3.2 The Doctor came asking to take her to Snezhnaya. Tighnari refused ("rude and reckless") and later described a man so confident he seemed near insane, who treated him like "a talking rock". When Fatui troops came for her, Tighnari stood guard: "I may be staying at Pardis Dhyai as a scholar, but that doesn't mean I'm no longer a Forest Watcher." He and Dehya held them off until a living lightning storm from the Balladeer's Gnosis routed the Fatui and wounded Tighnari. He told the Traveler not to blame themselves.

7.content: In his Story Quest (Vulpes Zerda Chapter, 3.0) a contaminated zone in Avidya Forest led Tighnari and the Traveler to a mechanical crab stealing parts. It took them to the lab of Abattouy, an acquaintance from Tighnari's Akademiya days. Abattouy had been trying to make the crab, Karkata, truly alive, and had died from overcharged Ley Line extractors. Tighnari shut them down, buried him, destroyed most of the banned research so the Akademiya could not take it, and secretly repaired Karkata at Pardis Dhyai.

8.content: Kaveh asked Tighnari for ornamental plant advice for the Palace of Alcazarzaray and got help with other problems too; Tighnari also introduced him to Cyno. When Kaveh built a house over a Withering Zone, Tighnari invited him to dinner rather than holding it against him. Tighnari worries about Kaveh's debts and wonders whether living with Alhaitham is a blessing or a curse. He warns that Alhaitham operates on pure rationality; Alhaitham in turn defends Tighnari's character.
